blockerTaskBindings.principle: A blocked component is not a blocked task. A blocker binds the tasks whose own acceptance needs the inference source, the built shim binaries, or a redistributed third-party artefact. Dependency ordering in tasks.md is a planning fact and is not a rights question. This section is retained so the historical binding and its grounds stay auditable.

escalations.consequence: The grant and the condition must not be conflated. Section 2(a)(1) licenses reproduction and sharing 'for NonCommercial purposes only'. The recorded intended use of this project is private, local and non-commercial, so USING these weights on the owner's own machine is within the located grant, and it engages no ShareAlike condition because nothing is shared. REDISTRIBUTION is a separate act: placing the graphs in a shipped bundle is a Share, which triggers section 3(a) attribution, section 3(b) share-alike and the section 2(b)(3) royalty reservation, and it falls outside the recorded scope regardless of its non-commercial character. Separately, the TensorRT SLA and CUDA SLA each contain a clause (1.2.5) forbidding use of the SDK in a manner that would cause it to become subject to an open source software licence; whether a given arrangement of model weights and NVIDIA redistributables in one bundle engages that clause is likewise a question for the rights owner. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is not by itself a licence on the NVIDIA SDK - the two instruments govern different components - so no incompatibility is asserted.

escalations.finding: The TensorRT Supplement makes the runtime .so/.dll files distributable. trtexec.exe is a developer tool, and SLA 1.2.1.4 states that unless a developer tool is identified in the Agreement as distributable it is delivered for internal use only. The Agreement text located does not identify trtexec.exe as distributable.
escalations.consequence: The reference package ships trtexec.exe and its notice file claims the TensorRT redistributables come from NVIDIA's redistributable downloads under the same terms. That is the upstream author's reading, not a verified grant. Shipping trtexec.exe inside our bundle on the strength of that notice alone would be assuming a permission that has not been shown.
escalations.missingEvidence: written confirmation from NVIDIA that trtexec.exe may be redistributed, or a bundle design that does not ship it.
escalations.designNote: trtexec is only needed to build a TensorRT engine from an ONNX graph. The planned design builds engines in-process through the TensorRT builder API with an out-of-band preparation helper CLI. If that design holds, trtexec.exe is a build-time convenience and can stay out of the shipped bundle entirely - which resolves this by architecture rather than by permission. That is a design consequence to carry into M04/M15, not a legal finding.
escalations.resolution: RESOLVED BY ARCHITECTURE, NOT BY PERMISSION. Engines are built in-process through the TensorRT builder API with an out-of-band preparation helper, so trtexec.exe is a build-time convenience and never a run-time dependency. tool.trtexec is therefore redistribution 'external' and inBundle false: it is not shipped, and the Supplement's developer-tool restriction never engages.
escalations.whatDidNotChange: No written confirmation from NVIDIA was obtained, and none is required on this design. The upstream notice file's claim that the TensorRT redistributables may be redistributed does not extend to a developer tool, and this project does not rely on that claim.
escalations.note: This is a design consequence, and M04/M15 must hold it: if the design ever changes to shell out to trtexec.exe at run time, this resolution lapses and the component becomes blocked again until a design that omits it is restored or NVIDIA confirms in writing.

installedBundleInventory.digestSummary: Every one of the 83 digests was independently recomputed from the installed file and matched the manifest. 36 + 17 + 13 + 5 (this repository's own core, aji.dll, aji_trt.dll, mikai_native_prep.exe, mikai_native_verify.exe) + 1 (cudart) + 3 (TensorRT) + 3 (ORT/DirectML) + 4 (CRT) = 83. native_inspect.exe is the one binary with no independently recomputed input: it is a project-owned tool built by the root CMake in the Qt/MinGW cohort and its only prior copy in the SDK tree predates this build, so its provenance rests on codePaths plus the build record, not on a digest match.

installedBundleInventory.closureFinding: Every static import of every one of the 83 files resolves either inside the bundle, to an api-ms/ext-ms API set, or to a Windows system DLL. No file in the bundle imports a third-party DLL that the bundle does not ship, and none of the 80 DLLs imports libstdc++-6, libgcc_s_seh-1 or libwinpthread-1 - so the native closure cannot collide with the Qt GNU cohort. What the bundle DOES import from outside itself is named per row under importsNeedingAnExternalProvider, and every such name is a Windows system library or a driver-supplied library (nvcuda via the CUDA driver, Qt6Core for the project-owned inspect tool). That is a system dependency, not a missing third-party binary.
installedBundleInventory.selfContainmentLimit: ggml_backend_load_all resolves CPU backend DLLs by searching the executable's own directory and the current working directory, not via AddDllDirectory. The 14 ggml-cpu-*.dll files sitting beside the core is therefore necessary but NOT by itself proof that the variant set resolves on an arbitrary machine; that remains a run-time question and is not claimed here.
installedBundleInventory.escalationsUnchanged: ESC-1 (unlicensed upstream inference source), ESC-2 (CC BY-NC-SA spatial graphs, redistribution not cleared) and ESC-3 (RIFE whole-graph redistribution unresolved) are all still open. unknownsAndGaps: The Microsoft CRT EULA text was not recovered from the pinned installer payload, so the licence terms are identified by acquisition route only. Recorded as missing evidence, not as a grant.

The 13 relinked mpv-deps DLLs are export-identical to their prefix originals and byte-verified, but were built with --allow-multiple-definition and a statically linked private winpthread. Behavioural equivalence at run time is not proved and must not be inferred from the export comparison.

libmpv-2.dll statically imports vulkan-1.dll even though the meson option records vulkan=disabled. It is satisfied by the system Vulkan loader if one is present and is a soft dependency rather than a hard one, but its presence is recorded rather than assumed away.

The shipped bundle contains only the sm120 TensorRT builder resource, not the ptx and sm75-sm100 ones that buildConfigurationPins.CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES enumerates. On a GPU whose SM is not sm120 the builder would need the matching resource, which is absent from this bundle. That is a real closure gap for this particular installed instance and is recorded, not worked around.

models.* and the animejanai-onnx and rife graphs are user-supplied at run time and are deliberately NOT in the bundle; their ESC-2 and ESC-3 positions are recorded on their components and are unaffected by this inventory.

inBundleSemantics.meaning: inBundle answers 'may this component go into a DISTRIBUTABLE bundle?', not 'is this file present in the locally installed private bundle?'. The two differ for the blocked components and confusing them would either hide ESC-1 or pretend it away.
inBundleSemantics.privateInstalledInstance: The installed private bundle native-0.1.0-dev.2 does contain aji.dll and aji_trt.dll, built locally from the unlicensed upstream source. They are present for the owner's own private use and are marked inBundle false because no redistribution clearance exists for them.
inBundleSemantics.howToCheckPresence: installedBundleInventory.files[].componentId maps every one of the 83 installed files to its component, so presence and shipping decision are both explicit per file and neither has to be inferred from the other.
inBundleSemantics.unbuiltComponents: engine.aji-dml, tool.trtexec, models.animejanai-onnx and models.rife-v4.14 have no installed file at all: the DirectML interop proof was refused at run time and is recorded as an honest disabled capability, trtexec is omitted by architecture (ESC-5), and the model graphs are user-supplied at run time rather than shipped.
